note: Facts and sources behind the member descriptions in CO.json, gathered 2026-10-05. "review" holds research notes for a human check; "issues" lists open questions.

byways.name: Alpine Loop
byways.designation: Colorado Scenic and Historic Byway; BLM Back Country Byway
byways.where: Unpaved loop over Cinnamon and Engineer passes linking Lake City, Ouray and Silverton; Hinsdale, Ouray and San Juan counties

facts.fact: 63 miles; the two 12,000-foot passes, Cinnamon and Engineer, require a high-clearance four-wheel-drive vehicle; closed in winter.
The roads were first used by 19th-century miners hauling ore by mule-drawn wagon to Silverton, Ouray and Lake City.
Features include seven ghost towns and two high alpine passes.

byways.name: Cache la Poudre - North Park
byways.designation: Colorado Scenic and Historic Byway; National Forest Scenic Byway
byways.where: CO 14 from Fort Collins up Poudre Canyon over Cameron Pass to Walden; Larimer and Jackson counties

facts.fact: 101 miles linking Fort Collins with Walden in North Park, a bowl-shaped valley east of the Continental Divide.
The Cache la Poudre is Colorado's only federally designated National Wild and Scenic River.
At 10,276-foot Cameron Pass the highway meets Colorado State Forest; North Park has deer, antelope, elk, moose and beaver, and the Arapaho National Wildlife Refuge draws migrating waterfowl.

byways.name: Collegiate Peaks
byways.designation: Colorado Scenic and Historic Byway; Colorado Electric Byway
byways.where: US 24, US 285 and CO 291 along the upper Arkansas River through Buena Vista, Poncha Springs and Salida; Chaffee County

facts.fact: A paved 57-mile route along the foot of the Sawatch Range, most of it following the Arkansas River.
Aquamarine, the state gemstone, is mined on Mount Antero; the mining towns of Vicksburg, Winfield and St. Elmo are reachable from the byway.
Salida has the largest historic district in the state.

byways.name: Colorado River Headwaters
byways.designation: Colorado Scenic and Historic Byway; National Scenic Byway (2005); Colorado Electric Byway
byways.where: US 34, US 40 and county roads from Grand Lake by Granby and Kremmling to State Bridge; Grand and Eagle counties

facts.fact: 80 miles from Grand Lake, an old resort town on Colorado's largest natural lake, to State Bridge.
The route ends on a gravel road through Upper Gore Canyon; Kremmling to State Bridge is gravel with limited services.
Designated a National Scenic Byway in 2005.

byways.name: Dinosaur Diamond
byways.designation: Colorado Scenic and Historic Byway; National Scenic Byway (2002)
byways.where: CO 139, CO 64, US 40 and I-70 between Grand Junction, Fruita, Rangely and Dinosaur; continues as a loop through Utah

facts.fact: 134 miles in Colorado of a 486-mile loop through Colorado and Utah.
Features include Dinosaur National Monument, the Dinosaur Journey Museum, Colorado National Monument and the Canyon Pintado National Historic District.
Designated a National Scenic Byway in 2002; limited services on some stretches.

byways.review: Catalog lists it as a Utah byway; it is also a Colorado state byway.

byways.name: Flat Tops Trail
byways.designation: Colorado Scenic and Historic Byway; National Forest Scenic Byway; Colorado Electric Byway
byways.where: Rio Blanco CR 8 and Routt County roads over Ripple Creek and Dunkley passes between Meeker and Yampa

facts.fact: 82 miles between Meeker and Yampa through the original White River Plateau Timberland Reserve, set aside in the late 19th century.
Development was banned around Trappers Lake, called the 'Cradle of Wilderness'.
Still a working byway with mines, ranches and timber land; closed in winter near mile 31 on the west and at Dunkley Pass on the east.

byways.name: Frontier Pathways
byways.designation: Colorado Scenic and Historic Byway; National Scenic Byway (1998)
byways.where: CO 96 and CO 165 west from Pueblo to Westcliffe and Silver Cliff; Pueblo and Custer counties

facts.fact: 103 miles through the old frontier south of the Arkansas River, traveled first by the Ute and later by Spanish and American explorers, trappers and ranchers.
Westcliffe and Silver Cliff in the Wet Mountain Valley are an International Dark Sky Community.
Designated a National Scenic Byway in 1998.

byways.name: Gold Belt Tour
byways.designation: Colorado Scenic and Historic Byway (1989); BLM Back Country Byway (1989); National Scenic Byway (2000); Colorado Electric Byway (2024)
byways.where: Phantom Canyon Road, Shelf Road, High Park Road, CO 9 and US 50 linking Cripple Creek, Victor, Cañon City, Florence and Florissant; Teller and Fremont counties

facts.fact: 131 miles; Cripple Creek and Victor were the heart of the 1890s gold boom and mining continues today.
Phantom Canyon Road follows a former ore railroad that climbed 4,550 feet in 30 miles, with two tunnels cut through granite and the 1897 Steel Bridge.
Shelf Road was built as a toll road in 1892; one stretch clings to a canyon wall 200 feet above the stream bed.

byways.name: Grand Mesa
byways.designation: Colorado Scenic and Historic Byway; National Scenic Byway (1996); National Forest Scenic Byway; Colorado Electric Byway
byways.where: CO 65 from I-70 at Plateau Creek over the Grand Mesa to Cedaredge; Mesa and Delta counties

facts.fact: 63 miles from I-70 up the canyon of Plateau Creek to forest 11,000 feet above sea level.
More than 300 stream-fed lakes hold rainbow, cutthroat and brook trout; Land's End Overlook stands on the mesa.
Designated a National Scenic Byway in 1996; services between Cedaredge and Mesa are limited.

byways.name: Guanella Pass
byways.designation: Colorado Scenic and Historic Byway; National Forest Scenic Byway
byways.where: Guanella Pass Road (Clear Creek CR 381 / Park County CR 62) between Georgetown and Grant; Clear Creek and Park counties

facts.fact: 22 miles over the divide between the South Platte and Clear Creek watersheds, cresting above timberline.
Lower slopes carry spruce, fir, aspen and pine; higher up, streams wind through meadows with beaver; Mount Bierstadt flanks the road, and Georgetown and Silver Plume lie at the north end.
Seasonally closed about Nov. 26 to Memorial Day weekend at Naylor Lake and Burning Bear Campground.

byways.review: Grant as the south end and the Park County road number are not on the CDOT page; the GIS line is labelled route 381.

byways.name: Highway of Legends
byways.designation: Colorado Scenic and Historic Byway; National Scenic Byway (2021); National Forest Scenic Byway; Colorado Electric Byway
byways.where: CO 12 from Trinidad over Cuchara Pass to US 160 near Walsenburg, with an extension on Huerfano/Las Animas CR 46 over Cordova Pass from Aguilar

facts.fact: 82 miles through country of the Sangre de Cristos, the Spanish Peaks and the red rock walls of the Dakota Wall and the Devil's Stairsteps.
A 35-mile extension follows County Road 46 from Aguilar over 11,248-foot Cordova Pass to CO 12 at Cuchara Pass; part of it is gravel and closed in winter.
Designated a National Scenic Byway in 2021.

byways.review: CDOT says national designation came in 2021; the catalog does not list it as a National Scenic Byway.

byways.name: Lariat Loop
byways.designation: Colorado Scenic and Historic Byway; National Scenic Byway; Colorado Electric Byway
byways.where: US 6, CO 74, CO 8 and the Lariat Trail (Lookout Mountain Road) linking Golden, Morrison and Evergreen; Jefferson County

facts.fact: A 40-mile route connecting Golden, Morrison and Evergreen in the foothills west of Denver.
It crosses Lookout Mountain on the five-mile Lariat Trail.
Features include Red Rocks Park and Amphitheatre, the Buffalo Bill Museum and Grave, Dinosaur Ridge and the Boettcher Mansion.

byways.name: Los Caminos Antiguos
byways.designation: Colorado Scenic and Historic Byway
byways.where: CO 150, US 160, CO 159, CO 142, US 285 and CO 17 across the San Luis Valley from Great Sand Dunes to Antonito and Cumbres Pass; Alamosa, Costilla and Conejos counties

facts.fact: 129 miles across the San Luis Valley between the Sangre de Cristo Range and the San Juan foothills.
Passes San Luis (1851), Colorado's oldest surviving community, its oldest parish, Our Lady of Guadalupe in Conejos, and Fort Garland, one of its first military posts.
Features include Great Sand Dunes National Park, Zapata Falls and the Cumbres & Toltec Scenic Railroad.

byways.review: Catalog also lists this as a BLM Back Country Byway; CDOT says the state system includes only two BLM Back Country Byways, and its pages name only Alpine Loop and Gold Belt as such. Worth checking.

byways.name: Mount Blue Sky (formerly Mount Evans)
byways.designation: Colorado Scenic and Historic Byway; National Forest Scenic Byway
byways.where: CO 103 from Idaho Springs to Echo Lake, CO 5 to the summit, and Clear Creek CR 103 / Jefferson CR 66 to Bergen Park; Clear Creek and Jefferson counties

facts.fact: The road climbs more than 7,000 feet in 28 miles to 14,130 feet, above timberline among mountain goats, pikas, marmots and alpine lakes.
The eastern part runs from Echo Lake to Bergen Park on Clear Creek County Road 103 and Jefferson County Road 66; total length 49 miles.
The road from Echo Lake Lodge to the summit is open roughly Memorial Day to Labor Day and vehicle entry requires a reservation on recreation.gov.

byways.review: Renamed Mount Blue Sky in 2023; catalog still uses Mount Evans and maps only 28 miles, while CDOT gives 49 miles including the Echo Lake to Bergen Park leg.

byways.name: Pawnee Pioneer Trails
byways.designation: Colorado Scenic and Historic Byway
byways.where: CO 14, CO 52 and county roads across the Pawnee National Grassland and the plains around Sterling and Fort Morgan; Weld, Morgan and Logan counties

facts.fact: 128 miles across the Colorado Piedmont, anchored by the Pawnee Buttes.
The shortgrass prairie is home to coyotes, prairie dogs, pronghorn and hundreds of bird species.
Unpaved county roads carry heavy truck traffic; watch for flying dirt and rocks.

byways.name: Peak to Peak
byways.designation: Colorado Scenic and Historic Byway; National Forest Scenic Byway
byways.where: CO 7, CO 72 and CO 119 from Estes Park through Nederland to Black Hawk; Larimer, Boulder and Gilpin counties

facts.fact: Established in 1918, it is Colorado's oldest scenic byway; 55 miles long.
Gravel side roads lead to high lakes, trailheads, the Moffat Tunnel's east portal and the ghost towns of Hesse and Apex.
The Peak to Peak Highway connects to Trail Ridge Road at Estes Park; it runs through Gilpin, Boulder and Larimer counties.

byways.name: San Juan Skyway
byways.designation: Colorado Scenic and Historic Byway; All-American Road (1996); National Forest Scenic Byway
byways.where: Loop on US 550, US 160, CO 145 and CO 62 through Durango, Silverton, Ouray, Ridgway, Telluride and Cortez

facts.fact: A 236-mile loop through Durango, Telluride, Silverton and Ouray.
The segment from Ouray to Silverton is called the Million Dollar Highway.
Passes Mesa Verde National Park; designated an All-American Road in 1996.

byways.name: Santa Fe Trail
byways.designation: Colorado Scenic and Historic Byway; National Scenic Byway (1998)
byways.where: US 50 along the Arkansas River from the Kansas line by Lamar and La Junta, then US 350 to Trinidad and I-25 to Raton Pass; continues into New Mexico

facts.fact: A 188-mile Colorado portion of the trail (565 miles across Colorado and New Mexico); the trade route saw its heaviest use between the 1820s and 1870s.
On a clear spring day the wagon-wheel ruts can still be seen on the prairie; the Mountain Branch ran through Trinidad and over Raton Pass.
The byway's midpoint is Bent's Old Fort, once a trading post and now a National Historic Site.

byways.review: Catalog does not list the Colorado state designation.

byways.name: Silver Thread
byways.designation: Colorado Scenic and Historic Byway; National Scenic Byway (2021); National Forest Scenic Byway; Colorado Electric Byway
byways.where: CO 149 from South Fork through Creede and Lake City to US 50 at Blue Mesa Reservoir; Rio Grande, Mineral, Hinsdale and Gunnison counties

facts.fact: 117 miles; between Creede and Lake City, CO 149 follows the upper Rio Grande past North Clear Creek Falls and the Slumgullion earth slide.
The byway was extended north from Lake City to Blue Mesa Reservoir at US 50.
Designated a National Scenic Byway in 2021.

byways.review: CDOT says national designation came in 2021; the catalog does not list it as a National Scenic Byway.

byways.name: South Platte River Trail
byways.designation: Colorado Scenic and Historic Byway
byways.where: Loop on I-76, US 138, US 385 and Sedgwick County roads around Julesburg; Sedgwick County

facts.fact: A 19-mile loop starting at the Colorado Welcome Center in Julesburg; the shortest of Colorado's 26 byways.
Interpretive signs mark the original Julesburg townsite, Colorado's only Pony Express home station, and Fort Sedgwick, established in 1864.
Markers also commemorate the other three Julesburg townsites, the Transcontinental Railroad and the Lincoln Highway.

byways.name: Top of the Rockies
byways.designation: Colorado Scenic and Historic Byway; National Scenic Byway (1998); Colorado Electric Byway
byways.where: US 24, CO 91 and CO 82 linking Minturn, Leadville, Copper Mountain, Twin Lakes and Aspen over Tennessee, Fremont and Independence passes

facts.fact: Leadville, at 10,200 feet, is the highest incorporated community in the United States; Mount Elbert and Mount Massive stand south of town.
The 115-mile route crosses the Continental Divide three times and follows the Arkansas River nearly to its source near Fremont Pass.
An extension runs from Twin Lakes over 12,095-foot Independence Pass on CO 82 into Aspen.

byways.review: CDOT says 115 miles and also describes a 40-mile Independence Pass extension; check that the catalog line includes CO 82 from Twin Lakes to Aspen (the CDOT GIS layer does).

byways.name: Tracks Across Borders
byways.designation: Colorado Scenic and Historic Byway
byways.where: CO 172, CO 151, US 160 and county roads from Durango through Ignacio and Arboles toward Chama, NM; La Plata and Archuleta counties

facts.fact: 89 miles in Colorado (125 miles total to Chama, New Mexico), along the Colorado-New Mexico border.

The main theme is the Denver and Rio Grande narrow gauge railroad; the route passes through Southern Ute Indian Tribe reservation land, with the tribe's headquarters and the Southern Ute Cultural Center and Museum in Ignacio.
It skirts the north end of Navajo Lake and has a round-trip spur to Chimney Rock National Monument; signage and visitor facilities are still being installed.

byways.review: Not in the catalog. Newest byway; CDOT says implementation (signage, turnouts) is still underway. Visitors are asked to respect tribal land and private property.

byways.name: Trail of the Ancients
byways.designation: Colorado Scenic and Historic Byway; National Scenic Byway (2005)
byways.where: US 160, US 491, CO 184, CO 41 and county roads around Cortez and Dolores to Hovenweep and Four Corners; Montezuma County; continues into Utah

facts.fact: A 116-mile Colorado route (480 miles with Utah) across the homeland of the Ancestral Puebloans; designated a National Scenic Byway in 2005.
Attractions include Hovenweep National Monument, Mesa Verde National Park, Yucca House and the Canyons of the Ancients National Monument visitor center in Dolores.
The byway won a 2020 National Scenic Byway Foundation award for the McElmo Creek Flume restoration; some roads are gravel and muddy when wet.

byways.review: Catalog does not list the Colorado state designation.

byways.name: Trail Ridge Road: Rocky Mountain National Park
byways.designation: Colorado Scenic and Historic Byway; All-American Road (1996); Colorado Electric Byway
byways.where: US 34 through Rocky Mountain National Park between Estes Park and Grand Lake

facts.fact: 48 miles; the road reaches 12,183 feet and is higher than any other paved through-road in the country.
Wildflowers cover the tundra in midsummer, and elk and bighorn sheep cross the meadows.
Designated an All-American Road in 1996; the high section normally opens by Memorial Day weekend.

byways.review: Catalog name is Trail Ridge Road/Beaver Meadow Road; CDOT page still shows the 2023 timed-entry notice.

byways.name: Unaweep/Tabeguache
byways.designation: Colorado Scenic and Historic Byway
byways.where: CO 141 from Whitewater through Unaweep Canyon, Gateway and Uravan, then CO 145 to Placerville; Mesa, Montrose and San Miguel counties

facts.fact: 133 miles on Highways 141 and 145; Unaweep Canyon cuts through red sandstone of the Uncompahgre Plateau down to Precambrian rock.
A copper boom came around 1900, and later the U.S. Army processed ore from nearby Uravan for uranium used in the first atomic bombs.
Features include the Hanging Flume, Driggs Mansion, the Gateway Colorado Auto Museum and the Dolores and San Miguel rivers.

byways.name: West Elk Loop
byways.designation: Colorado Scenic and Historic Byway; National Forest Scenic Byway
byways.where: CO 133, CO 92, US 50, CO 135 and Gunnison County Road 12 over Kebler Pass, linking Carbondale, Paonia, Hotchkiss, Crawford, Gunnison and Crested Butte

facts.fact: 205 miles anchored by Mount Sopris and the Black Canyon of the Gunnison.
The coke ovens at Redstone remain; towns include Carbondale, Hotchkiss, Crawford, Gunnison and Crested Butte.
A 31-mile gravel section over Kebler Pass is closed in winter.

byways.review: 'ranch towns' rests on CDOT's line that settlers stayed to farm and ranch.

issues: Tracks Across Borders (Durango to Chama, NM) is not in the catalog; drawable from the CDOT layer with NAME = 'Tracks Across Borders'. CDOT says signage and facilities are still being installed.

Mount Evans was renamed Mount Blue Sky in 2023; CDOT page title says 'Mount Blue Sky (formerly Mount Evans)' and its slug still says mount-evans. Catalog name is stale. Catalog maps 28 miles; CDOT gives 49 miles including Echo Lake to Bergen Park (CR 103/CR 66).
Highway of Legends and Silver Thread became National Scenic Byways in 2021 per CDOT; catalog lacks the National Scenic Byway designation for both. CDOT counts 13 America's Byways in Colorado.
Catalog lacks the Colorado state designation on Dinosaur Diamond, Santa Fe Trail, Trail of the Ancients and Trail Ridge Road, though all four are among CDOT's 26.

Catalog lists Los Caminos Antiguos as a BLM Back Country Byway, but CDOT says the state system has only two BLM Back Country Byways and only names Alpine Loop and Gold Belt as such on their pages. Check whether Los Caminos still carries the BLM designation.
Top of the Rockies: CDOT text gives 115 miles and separately a 40-mile Independence Pass extension to Aspen; confirm the catalog line includes CO 82 Twin Lakes to Aspen.
Highway of Legends: confirm the catalog line includes the Cordova Pass extension on CR 46 from Aguilar (the CDOT layer does).
Trail Ridge Road CDOT page still shows a 2023 timed-entry notice (stale). Mount Blue Sky page notes the summit road reopens Memorial Day 2026 after construction, with reservations required.
CDOT overview notes a moratorium on new byway nominations.
